summary: Requires that the IETF never publish any IETF Stream RFC without IETF rough consensus. It updates RFC 2026, the document describing the standards process.

plainLanguage.summary: This Best Current Practice requires rough consensus before the IETF publishes an RFC on the IETF Stream. It updates the publication rules in RFC 2026.

subtitle: Requires rough consensus before publishing RFCs on the IETF Stream.

tldr.problem: RFC 2026 allowed some Informational or Experimental IETF Stream RFCs to be published without IETF rough consensus.
tldr.mechanism: RFC 8789 says the IETF must not publish an IETF Stream RFC without establishing rough consensus for publication.
tldr.outcome: The RFC updates RFC 2026 and points to the Independent and IRTF Streams for some documents without IETF consensus.

today: RFC 8789 is a Best Current Practice that updates RFC 2026. The unit metadata does not list it as obsoleted or updated.

sections.title: The Publication Gap
sections.content:
RFC 2026 allowed Informational or Experimental RFCs to be published without IETF rough consensus. That document was written before the separation of streams such as IRTF, IAB and Independent, when there was only one RFC series.

As a result, the IESG could approve an Internet-Draft for publication as an RFC without rough consensus.
sections.plainLanguage: The older publication rules predated separate streams. They allowed some IETF Stream RFCs to be published without rough consensus.

sections.title: The New Requirement
sections.content:
RFC 8789 requires that the IETF not publish RFCs on the IETF Stream without establishing IETF rough consensus for publication. The document updates RFC 2026 and describes this as the action it takes.

The RFC says it has no IANA actions. It also says it introduces no new security considerations, while noting that consensus on security aspects may potentially improve the security of IETF Stream documents.
sections.plainLanguage: An IETF Stream RFC needs rough consensus before publication. The document states this rule directly.

sections.title: Documents Without Rough Consensus
sections.content:
The RFC discusses a 2007 IESG statement requiring an IETF Last Call before a document was issued. It argues that documents were still published even after failing to achieve rough consensus.

For documents that the community cannot agree on, the RFC points to the Independent Stream. For research documents, it points to the IRTF Stream, which publishes minority-opinion Informational RFCs.
sections.plainLanguage: The RFC points to other streams for documents that lack IETF consensus. It names the Independent Stream and, for research, the IRTF Stream.
